title: Token-slot rendezvous synchronizer with NCCL sliding-window for overlap-friendly prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design and implement a token-slot rendezvous layer that decouples prefill and decode pacing across tensor/pipeline parallel stages and intentionally shapes NCCL communication into a sliding-window pattern to maximize kernel execution overlap. The feature targets heterogeneous clusters (mixed GPU types and NVLink topologies) and volatile request mixes (short chat vs long generation).

Motivation: Existing rendezvous points force tight synchrony between stages which results in idle compute or blocked NCCL transfers during prefill/decode waves. Prior work improved scheduling but focused on coarse microbatch timing. This ticket explores a slot-based rendezvous which: 1) allows lookahead bundling of tokens for early KV-cache population, 2) surfaces per-token kernel candidates (FP16/INT8/quantized kernels) to the conductor for opportunistic selection, and 3) coordinates NCCL slices into a sliding-window that trades peak bandwidth for sustained overlap with compute.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- 15-30% reduction in p95 and p99 tail latency for mixed short/long workloads vs master on a 4xV100 and 2xA100 heterogeneous cluster.
- 10-20% improvement in total tokens/sec (throughput) for a 90% long-generation workload.
- No customer-visible correctness regressions across our regression prompt set (eval-run id: eval-2025-02-22-slottest).

Design summary:
1) Token-slot rendezvous: each pipeline stage exposes a small ring of logical "slots" that can be filled by upstream microbatches. Slots carry metadata: sequence-length histogram, attention sparsity estimate, prefix cache keys, and a kernel-candidate list ranked by estimated wall-time.
2) Lookahead bundling: the scheduler can place several short sequences into a slot to batch KV-prefill and then scatter tokens into decode windows — preserves low latency for short chats while amortizing communication for longer sequences.
3) Kernel selection hints: runtime probes (lightweight perf counters gathered on representative batches) feed a scoring model that ranks kernels (fused attention, multi-head tiling, quantized matmul). The conductor uses score + slot urgency to pick kernels per-slot.
4) NCCL sliding-window: instead of firing all-reduce/collectives synchronously for a stage boundary, orchestrate staggered NCCL slices with controlled concurrency so transfers overlap with adjacent stage compute. This requires per-link bandwidth awareness and backpressure heuristics to avoid congestion.

Trade-offs considered:
- Increased scheduler complexity vs measurable perf gains. We prioritize incremental rollout behind flags.
- Potential for suboptimal kernel decisions on cold start; mitigated via online learning and a fast fallback to previous stable kernel.
- Memory overhead for slot metadata and extra KV bundling; bounded by slot count (default 4) and subject to per-GPU memory gating.

Phased plan:
- Spike (this ticket): prototype in user-space conductor with toggles for slot count, bundling threshold, and NCCL-slice-size. Run synthetic microbenchmarks and internal regression.
- Integration: port to runtime scheduler, add per-device topology probe and kernel-scoring micro-bench harness.
- Canary: enable for 10% of traffic in staging clusters for 48h with automated rollback if p50/p99 regress > 10%.

Instrumentation & observability:
- New metrics: slot_fill_rate, slot_starvation_count, kernel_select_latency, nccl_slice_queue_depth, nccl_overlap_ratio.
- Dashboards: grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/slots/slot-rendezvous (placeholder).
- E2E benchmark suite: perf-runner PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-runner/pull/431 (WIP).
